findings.title: Async legacy writes run on the request context, so they are cancelled once the request returns
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection launch the legacy write in a goroutine using a context derived from the request ctx (e.g. line 51 `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). The HTTP request context is cancelled when the handler returns, which happens right after the storage write succeeds. The legacy write will therefore often fail with context canceled, and the failure is only recorded in metrics. Legacy writes can silently be skipped, which defeats the purpose of mode 3's safety copy. The goroutine should use a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) plus the timeout.

findings.title: Object passed to the async legacy Create is shared with the storage Create and may be mutated concurrently
findings.body: The same `obj` is handed to d.Storage.Create (line 42) and then to d.Legacy.Create inside a goroutine (line 55). Storage create implementations typically mutate the object (set ResourceVersion, UID, creationTimestamp, name generation). The legacy goroutine therefore reads an object that may be written concurrently or is already modified, which is a data race and can write inconsistent data to legacy. The legacy path should get a DeepCopy taken before the goroutine starts, or the storage result should be used.

findings.title: Async legacy Update reuses objInfo that the storage Update has already consumed
findings.body: objInfo is passed to d.Storage.Update (line 126) and then reused in the legacy goroutine (line 139). UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is typically called once per store and may consume or mutate the old object; calling it concurrently from the goroutine races with the storage path. Also the legacy update may compute its update from a different base object than the one storage used, so the two stores can diverge without any error being surfaced.

findings.title: Storage Update failure is recorded as a legacy duration metric
findings.body: In the Update error path, the failure is recorded with d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) and startStorage, even though the failing call was the storage write. This corrupts legacy metrics and hides storage failures from the storage metric.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration and errors are recorded as storage metrics
findings.body: In the goroutine, the legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) (line 166) instead of recordLegacyDuration. Legacy failures are counted as storage and legacy metrics stay empty for this method.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses the object name in the kind label position
findings.body: recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passes `name` where the other calls pass options.Kind. The kind label of the metric is therefore set to the object name, creating unbounded label cardinality and making the metric inconsistent with the other methods.

findings.title: Delete builds the context from d.Log, dropping the per-request log values
findings.body: Delete creates a local `log` with name/kind/method values but then attaches `d.Log` (line 97) to the context instead of `log`. Logs emitted by downstream code for delete lose the name, kind and method values that every other method attaches.

findings.title: Legacy write failures in async goroutines are not logged
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection run the legacy write in a goroutine and only record a metric on error. There is no log call, so a failed legacy write leaves no trace in logs and divergence between the stores is invisible to operators. The old code logged these failures, so this is a regression in observability.

findings.title: Update goroutine creates its timeout context before startLegacy and without a defer on the same line
findings.body: In the Update goroutine (lines 135-138) the timeout context is created before the timer starts and the cancel is deferred after an unrelated statement. This is harmless today but is inconsistent with the other goroutines and makes the cancel easy to miss if the function is edited. Low priority.

findings.title: Error test for Create passes only because the legacy expectation matches the storage call
findings.body: The 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case registers no storage expectation (setupStorageFn is nil). The storage Create call therefore matches the legacy mock expectation at line 41 and returns the error by accident. The test does not check what it claims to check, and a change in the call pattern would make it panic instead of asserting.

findings.title: Mode 3 tests never verify the asynchronous legacy write or wait for it
findings.body: The tests set legacy mock expectations but never assert they were called (AssertExpectations is not used), and the goroutines are not awaited. Tests pass even when legacy is never written, and goroutines can call mocks after the test has finished. The behavior that defines mode 3 (legacy write happens and does not fail the request) is not tested.

findings.title: Get test creates its own registry while the other tests share the package-level registry
findings.body: TestMode3_Get creates a new prometheus registry (line 119) while all other tests, and the mode1 test after this change, use the shared package-level `p`. Mixing the two patterns is inconsistent and makes it unclear whether the dual writer metrics are registered more than once on the shared registry across subtests.

findings.title: Mode 3 playlist integration tests check legacy consistency immediately after writes that are now asynchronous
findings.body: doPlaylistTests asserts legacy API results right after k8s creates, updates and deletes (for example the legacy list check after Create, and getFromBothAPIs after Update). With mode 3 the legacy write runs in a background goroutine, so these checks can race with it and fail intermittently. The new mode 3 subtests need a wait or retry before comparing the legacy store, or the assertions must be relaxed for mode 3.

findings.title: Unrelated module checksum entries added to go.work.sum
findings.body: The go.work.sum diff adds checksums for unrelated modules (grafana-azure-sdk-go/v2, prometheus-alertmanager, otel exporters, genproto rpc, etc.) that have nothing to do with the dual writer change. These look like incidental tooling output and should be removed from this PR to keep the change focused.
